title: Harness Engineering: The Operating System for Agentic AI
gist: BCG argues that as AI models commoditize, competitive advantage in agentic AI shifts to the 'harness' - a bespoke operating-system layer of specs, rules, audit controls, shared context, and quality gates wrapped around agents - citing a Southeast Asian bank (30%+ wealth-advisor revenue uplift, 4-5x conversion gains) and a software firm (5x team productivity) as proof points.

insights.claim: AI agents deployed in production are hallucinating, introducing workflow errors, falsely declaring tasks complete, and failing customer and regulatory scrutiny, and most large companies surveyed are not actively scaling agents, with those that do scale reporting limited bottom-line impact.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Investors should discount vendor claims of widespread enterprise agentic-AI adoption and near-term ROI until governance/control layers mature.
insights.quote: recent surveys indicate that most large companies are not actively scaling agents, and those that are report limited impact on the bottom line.
insights.locator: Yet the reality is that AI agents are hallucinating

insights.claim: As AI models become increasingly commoditized, competitive advantage in AI will not come from having the best underlying model but from building an effective 'harness' that encodes a company's specific processes, ways of working, and requirements.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Favor companies investing in proprietary process/governance layers around AI over those competing purely on model selection, since model choice is becoming a commodity input.
insights.quote: As AI models become increasingly commoditized, winning with AI won’t depend on having the best model.
insights.locator: As AI models become increasingly commoditized

themes.theme: Harness engineering as an operating system

insights.claim: Harness engineering is the practice of building an operating system around AI agents that establishes governance, accountability, and controls, analogous to how a PC's OS manages applications so they don't endanger the overall system and thereby creates user trust.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Assess AI vendors and internal deployments by the maturity of their control/governance layer, not just model quality, when judging real-world reliability.
insights.quote: This process, called harness engineering, establishes and ensures effective governance, accountability, and proper controls.
insights.locator: How can companies create agentic-driven processes

insights.claim: Even under a mature harness, human oversight remains a vital element of agentic systems; full autonomy is not the goal, supervised autonomy is.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Discount narratives of near-term full workforce replacement by agents; the realistic near-term model keeps humans in supervisory checkpoint roles.
insights.quote: Harness engineering works in a similar way, although human oversight remains a vital element.
insights.locator: How Harness Engineering Helped an Asian Bank

insights.claim: BCG built a fully agentic personalized-advisory platform for a large Southeast Asian bank spanning human-assisted and digital channels, which tripled the time wealth advisors spent actively engaging clients, delivered a 30%+ uplift in wealth-advisor revenue productivity, and produced a four-to-five-times improvement in customer conversion.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that harness-governed agentic deployments in regulated financial services can materially move advisor productivity and conversion metrics, a benchmark for evaluating similar bank AI rollouts.
insights.quote: The result was a 30%+ uplift in wealth-advisor revenue productivity, with associated four-to-five-times improvement in customer conversion.

insights.claim: In the bank deployment, engineering efficiency rose five-fold and speed from design to deployment improved 50%, and the author attributes these gains primarily to the harness (evaluation/approval processes and behavioral guardrails) rather than to the specific AI model chosen, which is what allowed the platform to run in a regulated banking environment.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: When diligencing AI-driven productivity claims, weight the governance/evaluation infrastructure behind a deployment more heavily than which foundation model is used.
insights.quote: These enhancements came less from the selected model and far more from the harness around it––the evaluation and approval processes and the behavioral guardrails.

insights.claim: A software company that shifted from using AI coding assistants/copilots to full harness engineering across its entire product development life cycle, from requirements through deployment and operations, increased team productivity by as much as five times.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Suggests the productivity ceiling from agentic AI in software development is far higher than from copilot-style assistants alone, relevant when modeling software-sector margin expansion from AI adoption.
insights.quote: we were able to increase the productivity of the team by as much as five times.
insights.locator: For example, we were recently employed by a software company

insights.claim: Regulators are moving away from principle-based guidance on AI agent use and toward architecture-based requirements, meaning companies will increasingly need to demonstrate specific technical controls rather than general policy statements.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Companies in regulated sectors should expect compliance costs to shift toward provable technical architecture (audit trails, control panels) rather than policy documents, favoring vendors who already build this in.
insights.quote: regulators are starting to move from principle-based guidance for the use of agents to architecture-based requirements.

insights.claim: Regulated industries such as financial services and telecommunications are particularly good fits for harness-engineered agents because their standards are already clear and well-documented, and a properly harnessed agent produces an audit trail by design rather than as an afterthought, helping meet compliance obligations.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Financial services and telecom incumbents may be able to adopt agentic AI faster and more defensibly than less-regulated sectors, an underappreciated first-mover advantage.
insights.quote: the agents produce an audit trail by design rather than as an afterthought, helping to meet compliance obligations.
insights.locator: Regulated industries are a particularly good fit

themes.theme: Five components of a harness operating system

insights.claim: Specs act as the overarching, machine-testable scope contract defining an AI system's purpose and boundaries with built-in evaluation criteria, functioning as the equivalent of an application manifest in a computer's operating system.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: When evaluating an enterprise's agentic AI maturity, check whether machine-testable scope/spec documents exist, not just prompts or policies.
insights.quote: The equivalent in a computer’s OS is the application manifest.
insights.locator: Specs. The specs are effectively the overarching scope contract

insights.claim: The constitution component sets deterministic, nonnegotiable rules for an agentic system covering mandatory actions, prohibited actions, escalation triggers, and individual accountability, functioning as the equivalent of the kernel in a computer's operating system.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: A named-accountability, deterministic rule layer is a due-diligence checkpoint for any regulated-industry agentic deployment.
insights.quote: The code used to write the constitution is deterministic, ensuring that its requirements are nonnegotiable.
insights.locator: Constitution. The constitution sets the specific rules

insights.claim: The control panel component gives human users visibility into what agents did, provides a proper audit trail, includes an escalation matrix, and offers failure-recovery options, functioning as the equivalent of the system monitor or process manager in a computer's operating system.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Audit-trail and failure-recovery tooling is a differentiator to look for in agentic AI vendors serving regulated clients.
insights.quote: It enables human users to see what the agents did and provides a proper audit trail, ensuring that all agentic actions are compliant with any regulations.
insights.locator: Control Panel. The control panel is similar to the system monitor

insights.claim: A rich context hub repository of a company's own background data and process knowledge prevents agents from confidently guessing or reaching out to unvetted external internet sources, and this proprietary context is what gives a company an edge over rivals, functioning as the equivalent of shared memory in a computer's operating system.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Proprietary data/context infrastructure, not the model itself, is the moat-relevant asset to value in an AI-native company.
insights.quote: It is this private context that gives players an edge over rivals.
insights.locator: Context Hub. Inadequate context is a key reason why agents fail

insights.claim: Effective harness engineering relies on four distinct quality-gate types operating together -- automated gates catching programmatic failures, evaluation gates where critic agents assess worker agents, human stage gates for named-individual sign-off, and regulatory gates ensuring compliance -- functioning as the equivalent of the system call and permissions layer in a computer's operating system.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: A common failure mode is treating all AI quality checks as equivalent; investors assessing an AI deployment's robustness should look for this four-tier gate structure specifically.
insights.locator: Quality Gates. A common mistake in agentic deployment

insights.claim: A governance 'maturity ladder' sets policy-agreed clearance rules by content risk level, so a client-facing investment proposal may require human approval of every output while battle-tested or low-risk internal content requires none, and this oversight burden is expected to shift over time from checking everything to spot-checking as trust in the agentic system grows.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Expect human-review costs in agentic AI deployments to decline over time as trust builds, which should be modeled as a declining opex line rather than a fixed cost.
insights.quote: As the outputs delivered by an agentic system become more trusted over time, the type of work involved is typically downgraded on the maturity ladder from “check everything” to “spot check now and then.”
insights.locator: A maturity ladder sets out the clearance rules

insights.claim: Based on experience in the banking industry, harness engineering disrupts traditional workforce pyramids that rely on a large base of junior staff, shifting organizational demand toward more senior, design- and strategy-focused roles.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Relevant to labor-cost and headcount-mix modeling for professional-services and banking firms adopting agentic AI: expect junior-role compression and senior-role growth rather than uniform headcount reduction.
insights.quote: these new structures disrupt traditional workforce pyramids, which contain a large base of junior staff, resulting in a shift toward more demanding design and strategy roles.
insights.locator: From our experience in the banking industry

insights.claim: Companies should start small with harness engineering, testing new approaches cautiously in real-world settings to ensure the harness's multiple interacting components work together before scaling up.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of enterprises claiming rapid, wholesale agentic rollouts without a staged pilot phase; the recommended path is incremental.
insights.quote: companies need to tread cautiously and test new approaches before scaling up.

insights.claim: Despite generic off-the-shelf harness platforms being available in the market, the author argues a bespoke, built-not-bought harness combined with an effective AI model creates a strong competitive moat because it encodes a company's own context, process logic, quality signals, and institutional knowledge that competitors cannot simply purchase and replicate.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Favor companies building proprietary harness/governance infrastructure over those buying generic AI-orchestration platforms off the shelf, as the latter is easier for competitors to replicate.
insights.quote: Together with an effective AI model, a customized harness can create a strong competitive moat.

insights.claim: Not every workflow is ready for agentic AI or harness engineering; the best early candidates are processes where the work is already documented, quality can be checked, and an agentic approach can be layered onto existing tools and systems.
insights.speaker: Aparna Kapoor
insights.so_what: Use documentation-quality and checkability as a screen for which of a company's business processes are realistic near-term agentic-AI ROI candidates.
insights.quote: The best early candidates are processes where the work is documented, quality can be checked, and an agentic approach can be applied to existing tools and systems.
